text:
The Rangers ended a four-game winless run at Madison Square Garden, and they did it behind Dylan Garand, a goalie the club drafted 103rd overall in 2020 and who was named the game's first star. He faced 33 shots and let in one, a late goal that mattered only to the scoreboard.

Our numbers say the Rangers earned it. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of shots, favored NYR 4.73 to 2.80, and in the simulated replays of every shot we use to judge who deserved to win, New York came out ahead 72 percent of the time. Shot attempts were nearly level (64 for NYR, 62 for STL), so the gap came from where the shots came from. The second period tilted it, with NYR out-chancing STL 2.12 to 1.13. Adam Fox, who was drafted 66th overall by Calgary and played at Harvard, broke the shutout early in that period with a snap shot. Oliver Bjorkstrand made it 2-0 in the third, and Eeli Tolvanen sealed it at 17:59 on a chance we rated at 55 percent.

St. Louis had its own help in goal. Joel Hofer stopped 28 of 30 and saved about 2.2 goals more than his workload deserved, which kept the game from getting away sooner. J.T. Miller had a 67 percent look stopped in the second. Neither team scored on the power play (STL 0 for 6, NYR 0 for 3). Pius Suter's backhand at 19:01, a 2 percent chance, was the only thing the Blues got past Garand. The Rangers leave with the winless run behind them. The Blues leave knowing a strong night in goal wasn't enough.
